newsitem.title: UK: Woollen tops sheared by sterling in Bradford.
newsitem.headline: Woollen tops sheared by sterling in Bradford.

text.p: Tops prices at the Bradford wool market were down across the board in thin trade on Thursday, industry sources said.
Finer tops lost between three and four pence per kg while even English types were quoted down a penny or two under the influence of the strong pound.
"Traders are increasingly worried about their ability to maintain healthy export margins," one market source said.
"If sterling had weakened instead of hitting new peaks over the holiday period, the prospect of higher prices for imported raw materials might have brought new covering business," he said.
Instead, easing in the major primary markets (except for the UK) has exacerbated the problem, encouraging buyers to hold back in expectation of lower prices.
Prices for 70s Super were down four pence per kg at 476 and 64s blended lost three at 387 pence.
